content: maxMemoryAllocationCount is a hard per-device cap (as low as 4096 on some GPUs/drivers) on live vkAllocateMemory calls; calling vkAllocateMemory per-resource exhausts it fast. The standard fix is suballocation -- allocate few large blocks and hand out sub-ranges -- but each sub-allocation must be contiguous (no multi-region resources) and bucketing by size class is needed to avoid fragmentation where free space exists in aggregate but not as one contiguous run large enough for a pending allocation.
